articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft just dropped patches for 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and a Windows Defender flaw called 'BlueHammer' — because apparently Redmond's April Fool's joke is pretending they care about security.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence turned old router vulns into a Microsoft Office token harvesting operation. When your IoT security is so bad it becomes a nation-state highway to corporate email — chef's kiss.

articles.title: Digital Hopes, Real Power: From Connection to Collective Action
articles.summary: FOIA requests exposed how ALPR surveillance actually works, so naturally states are now trying to classify the public records that reveal their digital dragnet. Can't have transparency ruining a perfectly good police state.

articles.title: Democratic Leaders Wanted to Control the Maine Senate Race. Their Pick Just Dropped Out.
articles.summary: Ron Wyden is making the NSA's lapdog Tom Cotton big mad by demanding transparency about secret court opinions. Cotton's threatening 'consequences' for constitutional oversight — how very democratic.

articles.title: The never-ending supply chain attacks worm into SAP npm packages, other dev tools
articles.summary: Mike Johnson bribed the Freedom Caucus with crypto provisions to pass domestic spy law reauthorization. Nothing says 'small government' like surveilling Americans while pumping digital tulips.

articles.title: PyTorch Lightning and Intercom-client Hit in Supply Chain Attacks to Steal Credentials
articles.summary: A 15-year-old allegedly breached France's secure document agency and leaked 18 million records. Teen shows government cybersecurity is about as robust as their wine regulations.

articles.title: Linux cryptographic code flaw offers fast route to root
articles.summary: New 'Copy Fail' Linux vulnerability lets unprivileged users become root across major distributions. Ten lines of exploit code and boom — you're God on the machine.

articles.title: Editorial. Challenge of Mythos
articles.summary: Microsoft's patch for that Russian-exploited zero-day was apparently written by interns because there's another Windows flaw under active attack. Patch Tuesday, meet Patch Every Damn Day.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after their 2022 SMS phishing spree. Another young talent gets processed by the justice system instead of hired by it.

articles.title: Wiz finds AI has moved from tool to infrastructure, broadening the attack surface
articles.summary: US-Estonian suspect Peter Stokes arrested in Finland over alleged Scattered Spider ties. International cybercrime manhunt or just another Tuesday in the proxy war economy.
